LanguageData.LW_Settings_EconomyDesc: Settlements grow, produce and consume goods, starve or prosper.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_DiplomacyDesc: Factions form alliances, declare war and make peace with each other.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_WarfareDesc: Factions at war send war bands against each other's settlements.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_ConquestDesc: Settlements can be captured or destroyed, and factions can be wiped out.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_TributariesDesc: When your people win an assault on a settlement, you may hold it instead of razing it: its people keep their homes and it becomes a free town allied to you, and its old masters will want it back. A held town pays you tribute (you set the rate) and may rise against you if pressed too hard. Off: a won assault destroys the town, as in vanilla. Towns you already hold stay as they are, but pay nothing and do not rise.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_ExpansionDesc: Prosperous factions send settlers to found new settlements.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_PartiesDesc: Merchants, war bands, settlers and envoys travel visibly across the world map.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_WarBandsDesc: When the storyteller sends a raid, a war band sets out from a hostile settlement and travels to your colony. You get a warning and can meet it on the way.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_MarketsDesc: Trade prices follow each settlement's supply and demand.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_FiguresDesc: Leaders, warlords and merchants with their own history, who come back to your colony.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_BordersDesc: Settlements claim the land around them. Factions whose lands touch grow rivalrous faster, new towns are only founded on free or their own land, and nobody settles inside your colony's reach. Off: the older rivalry by distance alone, and founding anywhere.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_TownMapsDesc: When you attack a town, its map reflects the town's state in the simulation: bigger towns have larger grounds, defenders follow how full its garrison is against what it wants, and loot follows its wealth. Quest settlements keep vanilla maps. Switch off for vanilla maps; maps already generated stay as they are.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_RoadsDesc: Towns that trade a lot build roads between them (and let them decay when the trade stops or war comes), and your caravans can build roads. A road joins your colony to the towns along it: their merchants and visitors come more often and think better of you. Built roads stay when this is switched off.
LanguageData.LW_Overlay_Mode_ShortageAnyTip: Each town's price factor over the goods it consumes, weighted by how much of each it consumes and never below 1: a scarce good shows in proportion to how much the town needs it.

LanguageData.LW_Markets_Help: What each nearby settlement pays, compared to the usual price. Red: they need it (sell to them). Green: they have plenty (buy there). Click a row to find the settlement.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_Help: Where goods sell best and which trips look worth making, from the nearest towns that will trade with you. Factors compare what you would pay or get with a normal price, with fame and fairs included, so they differ from the Prices view. Times are for a caravan leaving now. Click a row to find the settlement.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_OnlyHaveDesc: Under "Where to sell", list only goods the colony has stockpiled.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_ShowOnMapDesc: Shade the world map by where this good is in short supply, which is where it pays well.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_PricesOff: Dynamic market prices are switched off in the mod settings, so there is nothing to compare.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_NoColony: The colony is not on the planet's surface, so there is no road to plan from.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_Searching: Working out which towns can be reached...
LanguageData.LW_Routes_SellHelp: A comparison of markets, not a profit: what each town pays for a good, against a normal price.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_NoSell: No town nearby pays notably more than a normal price for these goods.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_RoutesHelp: Buy at one town, sell at another: the estimated profit after the usual trade markup, with your best negotiator.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_NoRoutes: No trip between these towns looks worth making right now.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_SellRow: {TOWN} pays ×{FACTOR} of a normal price for {GOOD}, {TIME}{ROAD}.{NOTE} You have {HAVE}.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_RouteRow: {REP}, bought at {BUY} and sold at {SELL}, est. +{PROFIT}% with {NEGOTIATOR}; {LEG1} + {LEG2}. {BUY} may not have it in stock.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_SellTip: The price you would get for a thing of this good, compared to a normal price, before your negotiator's bonus. The town never pays more for a thing than it would sell it for. Click to find the town.
LanguageData.LW_Routes_RouteTip: Worked out from the game's trade rules: you buy at 1.4 times a thing's value and sell at 0.6 times, each scaled by the town's market, the thing's own sell factor, the difficulty and your negotiator (the best one at home: colonists away with a caravan are not counted). What a town pays is held to what it would sell the thing for. A town's stock is never looked at, so check it when you arrive. Click to find the town to buy at.
LanguageData.LW_Career_PrinceSilver: {PAWN_nameDef}, merchant prince of {HOME}, brings a heavy purse: {SILVER} more silver to trade with.
LanguageData.LW_KinVisitText: {PARENT_nameFull} has come with the visitors from {HOME} to see {PARENT_possessive} child, {CHILD_nameDef}.
LanguageData.LW_KinDiedText: When {HOME} was razed, {PARENT_nameFull} died there. {CHILD_nameDef} has lost {CHILD_possessive} {PARENT_gender ? father : mother}.

LanguageData.LW_WarBandLedBy: Scouts say {PAWN_nameFull}, warlord of {HOME}, leads them in person: {PAWN_possessive} raid number {VISITS} on you. Kill or capture {PAWN_objective}, and {HOME} will feel it.

LanguageData.LW_RevengeIntro: {0} want revenge. Warriors from {ORIGIN} have sworn to avenge their fallen.

LanguageData.LW_RefugeesFromRazed: They had found shelter in {0}, until it was burned to the ground.

LanguageData.LW_Settings_PerfLogDesc: Writes one line per in-game day to a CSV file in the save-data folder (LivingWorld/perf-….csv): how long the day took in real seconds, the average cost of a tick and a frame, and the time spent in Living World's systems, all map components, Spaceports and Hospitality. Send the file to the mod author when reporting lag. Costs almost nothing; stays on until switched off and the game restarted.

LanguageData.LW_TributeText: A messenger from {ORIGIN} brings word from {FACTION}: pay {AMOUNT} silver, and they will leave your colony alone for a season.\n\nRefuse, and their warriors will come. The messenger waits two days; silence counts as a refusal.

LanguageData.LW_Envoy_Mission_PlayerPeace: Carrying your offer of peace to {0}.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_Intro: An envoy walks from your colony to {TOWN}, about {ETA} away, and brings their answer back. Current relations: {RELATION}.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_Chance: Chance they agree, as things stand now: {0}

LanguageData.LW_Dipl_PeaceGiftDesc: The gift goes with the envoy. If they refuse, they keep half of it (treacherous hosts may keep all of it, and the envoy).
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_PeaceNoGiftDesc: Weary, honourable factions with few grudges against you are most willing.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_CallDesc: As your allies, they may declare war (if not at war already) and attack the town of {0} nearest to you.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_TributeDesc: They are weaker than you. Paying or not, they will resent it (goodwill falls, more if they refuse).
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_NoOptions: There is nothing to ask of them now (a goodwill limit may keep them hostile). Peace can be offered to enemies, allies can be called to arms, and weaker factions can be made to pay tribute.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_Off: Diplomacy or world parties are switched off in this save

LanguageData.LW_Dipl_PeaceYesText: At {TOWN}, {FACTION} accepted your offer of peace and the gift of {SILVER} silver. They are no longer your enemies.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_PeaceNoText: At {TOWN}, {FACTION} heard your envoy out and sent them away, keeping {SILVER} silver of the gift for their trouble. The war goes on. Your envoy is walking home.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_PeaceNoTextNoGift: At {TOWN}, {FACTION} heard your envoy out and sent them away. The war goes on. Your envoy is walking home.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_PeaceMootText: By the time your envoy reached {TOWN}, {FACTION} were no longer at war with you. Your envoy is walking home.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_PeaceBlockedText: {FACTION} would have accepted, but something binds them to this war for now. Your envoy is walking home with the gift.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_EnvoyKilledText: At {TOWN}, {FACTION} took the gift of {SILVER} silver and killed your envoy. There will be no peace with them for now.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_CallYesText: {FACTION} answered your call. Their warriors are marching on {TARGET} of {ENEMY}.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_CallYesNoArmyText: {FACTION} answered your call and stand against {ENEMY}, but they have no warriors to spare just now.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_CallNoText: {FACTION} will not march against {ENEMY} for you, not now.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_CallMootLabel: Call to arms came to nothing: {0}
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_CallMootText: By the time your envoy reached {TOWN}, the call against {ENEMY} could no longer be answered.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_TributeYesText: At {TOWN}, {FACTION} gave in and handed over {SILVER} silver. Your envoy is bringing it home. They will not forget this.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_TributeNoText: At {TOWN}, {FACTION} refused to pay and sent your envoy away with insults.

LanguageData.LW_RaidersWeary: The raiders of {0} look tired of war. They may not fight to the last.
LanguageData.LW_RaidersHomeLost: The raiders of {0} have lost their home town. Their hearts are not in this fight.
LanguageData.LW_RaidersSworn: The raiders of {0} have sworn vengeance on your colony. They will not break easily.
LanguageData.LW_Reunion: {VISITOR_nameDef} and {COLONIST_nameDef} meet again and greet each other like old friends.
LanguageData.LW_RulerVisitsText: {PAWN_nameFull}, {TITLE} of {FACTION}, has come in person with the visitors from {HOME}.\n\nA ruler's visit is an honour. Treat {PAWN_objective} well — what happens to {PAWN_objective} here will be remembered.
LanguageData.LW_Audience_TradePact: {PAWN_nameDef} proposes a trade pact: for {DAYS} days their merchants come more often, and your name is better in all their towns.
LanguageData.LW_Audience_MarchWithUs: {PAWN_nameDef} asks you to march with them against {ENEMY}: destroy {TARGET}, and they will pay you well.
LanguageData.LW_Audience_SettleNearby: {PAWN_nameDef} asks your leave to found a town of their people near your colony. A friendly neighbour, and a debt of gratitude.
LanguageData.LW_Audience_Gift: {PAWN_nameDef} brings a gift of {SILVER} silver as a sign of friendship.
LanguageData.LW_Audience_Supports: {PAWN_nameDef} is for it: {PAWN_possessive} people live in {HOME}.
LanguageData.LW_Audience_MarchAccepted: You promised to destroy {0}. Do it within 30 days and they will pay {1} silver.
LanguageData.LW_Plea_BuyFoodText: The visitors from {HOME} ({FACTION}) say their town is going hungry. They ask to buy {COUNT} meals from your stores, and {FACTION} will pay {SILVER} silver for them — more than the market.\n\nThe food goes home with them; {HOME} will remember who helped.
LanguageData.LW_Plea_RefugeLabel: A visitor from {0} asks to stay
LanguageData.LW_Plea_RefugeText: {PAWN_nameFull} came with the visitors from {HOME} ({FACTION}). Raiders sacked {HOME} days ago, and {PAWN_pronoun} has nothing to go back to.\n\n{PAWN_pronoun} asks to stay and join your colony.
LanguageData.LW_Plea_MercenaryLabel: Visitors from {0} want to hire a fighter
LanguageData.LW_Plea_MercenaryText: The visitors from {HOME} ({FACTION}) say their town is at war and short of fighters. They ask whether {PAWN_nameDef} would come back with them and fight for a few days, for {SILVER} silver and a share of the plunder.\n\n{PAWN_pronoun} would travel to {HOME} and return when it is over — most likely richer, perhaps wounded, possibly not at all.
LanguageData.LW_Merc_SetOut: {PAWN_nameDef} sets out to fight for {TOWN}; about {ETA} to get there.
LanguageData.LW_Merc_Paid: {PAWN_nameDef} fought for {TOWN} and came through unharmed. {PAWN_pronoun} is on the way home with {SILVER} silver in pay and plunder.
LanguageData.LW_Merc_Wounded: {PAWN_nameDef} fought for {TOWN} and was wounded. {PAWN_possessive} wounds were dressed in the field; {PAWN_pronoun} is on the way home with {SILVER} silver. Let {PAWN_objective} rest when {PAWN_pronoun} arrives.
LanguageData.LW_Merc_Killed: {PAWN_nameDef} fell fighting for {TOWN}. {TOWN} sends {PAWN_possessive} body home with {SILVER} silver.
LanguageData.LW_Merc_TurnedBack: {PAWN_nameDef} found no one to fight for at {TOWN} (the town changed hands, or its people turned on the colony) and is coming home unpaid.
LanguageData.LW_Merc_Back: {PAWN_nameDef} is back from the fighting abroad.
LanguageData.LW_Merc_CannotGo: {PAWN_nameDef} cannot set out now (drafted, not in the colony, or the town is gone).
LanguageData.LW_PartyStrandedText: {PAWN_nameDef} was on the way home, but the colony's home is gone. {PAWN_pronoun} goes on as a caravan from where {PAWN_pronoun} stands.
LanguageData.LW_Envoy_Mission_PlayerMercenary: Taking a fighter of yours to {0}.
LanguageData.LW_Commission_OfferText: {PAWN_nameFull} says {HOME} is short of goods and asks whether your colony could make {COUNT} {THING} for {PAWN_objective} to collect on {PAWN_possessive} next visit, in about {DAYS} days.\n\n{PAWN_pronoun} offers {SILVER} silver for them — more than the market pays. Forbid them once made, so your colonists don't use them up; they are handed over all the same.
LanguageData.LW_Commission_Accept: Take the order ({0} silver on delivery)
LanguageData.LW_Commission_DeliveryText: {PAWN_nameFull} has come to collect the {COUNT} {THING} you promised, and brings {SILVER} silver.
LanguageData.LW_Commission_NotYet: {PAWN_nameDef} asks after the {COUNT} {THING}; it is not due yet, and {PAWN_pronoun} will come back for it.
LanguageData.LW_Commission_Missing: {PAWN_nameDef} came for {COUNT} {THING}, but your stores do not have them. {PAWN_pronoun} leaves disappointed.
LanguageData.LW_Inspect_Story_KinExecuted: one of theirs died your prisoner
LanguageData.LW_Legends_RenownTip: Your name travels: friendly neighbours visit {0}% more often, and merchants who know you place orders more readily.
LanguageData.LW_Legends_None: The colony's legend is yet to be written.
LanguageData.LW_Deed_FeudEnded: ended the blood feud: slew {0}, who had sworn to avenge {1}
LanguageData.LW_Grudge_BloodPrice: took a blood price from the colony

LanguageData.LW_Dipl_WeregildDesc: End the blood feuds sworn against your colonists: {0}. If they take the silver, the oaths are renounced and old grudges ease; if not, your envoy brings it home.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_WeregildYesText: {FACTION} took {SILVER} silver at {TOWN} as the blood price. {TARGET} has renounced the oath; the feud is over.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_WeregildNoText: {FACTION} will not sell their dead. Your envoy leaves {TOWN} with the {SILVER} silver; the feud goes on.
LanguageData.LW_Dipl_WeregildMootText: By the time your envoy reached {TOWN}, no one of {FACTION} was sworn against your colony any more. The {SILVER} silver comes home.
LanguageData.LW_Settings_HireBandsDesc: Pay a faction that is not your enemy, and is already at war with one of yours, to send a war band against one of that enemy's towns. Needs faction diplomacy, parties on the world map and warfare between factions as well. Off: nothing can be hired, and a hire whose envoy has not yet answered comes to nothing (the silver comes home). A band already marching still fights.

LanguageData.LW_Hold_Text: The last defenders of {TOWN} have fallen or fled. About {POP} people still live there. Raze it as conquerors do, or hold it: its people keep their homes and become a free town, as friendly to you as it can be (an ally, when nothing stands in the way), and its old masters will want it back. It will pay you tribute every {DAYS} days, and if you press it too hard it may rise against you. You cannot settle on a town you hold.
